class.name: SpatialCable
class.brief_description: A procedurally meshed, wind-driven cable strung between two points.
class.description: Runs one or more parallel strands between endpoint A (this node's origin plus [member start_position], or the node at [member attach_start]) and endpoint B ([member end_position], or [member attach_end]). Each strand is a Verlet particle chain: pinned at both anchors, pulled by [member gravity], pushed by a gusting wind vector and given a subtle idle sway. The visible geometry is a round tube ([member cable_sides] around, [member cable_segments] along) rebuilt every frame into an internal [ImmediateGeometry]; it takes an ordinary [member material] and honours [member cast_shadow]. When [member collision_enabled] is set the cable owns an internal [StaticBody] of capsule segments on [member collision_layer], so hitscan rays collide with it — call [method hit] with the collision point to sever it. With [member detect_shots] the cable also watches the [member projectile_group] node group itself and severs on contact. A severed segment splits the strand; each half keeps hanging from the anchor it still holds. The node is fully live in the editor (static resting curve, no dynamics).

method.name: get_point_count
method.description: Number of simulated particles per strand ([member cable_segments] + 1).

method.name: get_point_position
method.description: World-space position of one simulated particle. Useful for attaching effects or a hanging object to the cable.

method.name: hit
method.description: Registers a hit at a world-space point. Emits [signal cable_hit]; when [member breakable] is set, also cuts the nearest strand segment and emits [signal cable_severed]. Call this from your weapon code with the raycast's collision point.

method.name: is_severed
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if any strand segment is currently cut.

method.name: rebuild
method.description: Rebuilds strand and collision topology immediately. Only needed after changing [member cable_count] or [member cable_segments] from a tool script mid-frame; the Inspector does it automatically.

method.name: reset_cable
method.description: Rejoins every cut and snaps all strands back to their resting curve.

method.name: sever
method.description: Cuts one specific strand segment directly. [code]segment_index[/code] runs [code]0[/code] to [member cable_segments] [code]- 1[/code].

members.member: If set to a valid [Spatial], endpoint B tracks that node's global origin and [member end_position] is ignored.
If set to a valid [Spatial], endpoint A tracks that node's global origin and [member start_position] is ignored.
If [code]false[/code], [method hit] and shot detection still emit [signal cable_hit] but never cut the cable.
Number of parallel strands run between the two endpoints. Changing this rebuilds the simulation.
Tube radius of each strand, in metres.
Number of segments along each strand — more segments give a smoother curve and finer breaks, at higher cost. Changing this rebuilds the simulation.
Number of sides around the tube cross-section.
Extra strand length as a fraction of the straight-line distance between endpoints. [code]0[/code] is taut; higher sags more.
Distance between adjacent parallel strands. They are spread along the horizontal axis perpendicular to the line between the endpoints.
Whether the cable mesh casts shadows.
Builds an internal [StaticBody] of capsule segments that follow the cable, so raycasts and physics bodies collide with it.
Physics layer of the internal collision body.
Physics mask of the internal collision body.
Velocity lost per step. Higher settles the cable faster and kills jitter; too high looks like it moves through syrup.

If set, each physics frame the cable checks every node in [member projectile_group] against its strands (sweeping the node's motion since last frame so fast rounds do not tunnel) and calls [method hit] on contact. No weapon-side code needed.
Endpoint B, in this node's local space. Ignored when [member attach_end] resolves to a node.
Downward acceleration on the strand particles.
Extra distance (added to [member cable_radius]) within which a [member projectile_group] node counts as hitting the cable.
Material applied to the cable mesh (as a material override). [code]UV.x[/code] wraps around the tube, [code]UV.y[/code] runs along its length.
Node group scanned when [member detect_shots] is set. Put your bullets / pellets in this group.
Runs the Verlet dynamics at runtime. When [code]false[/code] the cable holds its resting curve (still follows moving endpoints, still breakable). Always [code]false[/code] in the editor.
Distance-constraint relaxation passes per step. Higher is stiffer and less stretchy.
Endpoint A, in this node's local space. Ignored when [member attach_start] resolves to a node.
Strength of each constraint correction, [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code]. Lower makes a stretchier, more elastic cable.
Physics substeps per frame. Raise for very long or very taut cables that jitter.
Amplitude of the built-in idle sway — a gentle sideways oscillation applied even with no wind. Set to [code]0[/code] to disable.
Enables the built-in idle sway.
Frequency of the idle sway.
Per-cable multiplier on how strongly this cable responds to the wind — a light wire flutters more than a heavy hawser. [code]0[/code] ignores wind entirely.
World-space direction the wind blows. Normalised internally.
Enables the wind force on the strands.
Base wind acceleration before gusts and [member wind_affect].
Gustiness. [code]0[/code] is a steady wind; higher swings the wind force up and down over time, each strand slightly out of phase.

signal.name: cable_hit
signal.description: Emitted by [method hit] and by shot detection whenever the cable is struck, whether or not it breaks.

signal.name: cable_severed
signal.description: Emitted when a strand segment is cut (by [method hit], [method sever] or shot detection).
